verdict: This one would make me lean forward, and not because of the bloom. The three must-haves of PS 4.2 are met literally (JSON of top-100 products + pick counts + order list; grid warehouse with racks, aisles, dock, animated picker walking an aisle graph with live distance/time counters; swap-or-drag game with same-orders replay, before/after km and pick time, and a fast-movers-nearest-dock baseline), all three watch-outs are mapped to specific code (C-invoice and non-product-code filtering in prep.py with counts, graph-constrained paths, instanced geometry with a quality toggle), and every visual element I probed is driven by the simulation output rather than painted on: the path is the routed node sequence, floor heat is visits, box colour is pick frequency, the ghost is the old layout's path on the same orders, affinity links are co-occurrence counts. The headless simulate() shared by scoring, animation, baseline, annealer and `npm run eval` is the right architecture and the chronological split with hyperparameters frozen before the test run is more honesty than 25 of the 30 teams will show. Zero-backend static hosting removes every flaky dependency I have watched kill demos. Where it is weaker: the 5-minute script is packed to the second with four wow moments, a trackpad handoff and a 10 s live anneal, which in practice means the ghost race or the leaderboard gets cut; the headline "-30%" is player-vs-random, a straw man any logistics judge will call out, while the number that actually proves the AI (annealed vs the brief's baseline) is unmeasured and may be a few percent under exact single-order routing; the "where is the AI" question at an AI hackathon lands on a search heuristic, which is a fine answer only if it is delivered with a measured gain; and the team will be explaining 3,000 lines of agent-written TypeScript on no sleep. None of this is structural. Build it, measure SA-vs-baseline by hour 4, cut the script to three beats, and this is a top-3 entry.
weaknesses: Headline number is a straw man: 'Ghost 18.4 km / You 12.9 km / -30%' compares the player against a seeded RANDOM slotting. No real warehouse is random. The number that proves the AI is Annealed vs the brief's own baseline (fast movers nearest the dock), and under exact Held-Karp routing with single-order picking and ~3-5 covered lines per order, affinity slotting over frequency slotting typically yields single-digit percent (Petersen & Aase 2004 show class/volume-based storage captures most of the benefit). If SA-vs-baseline comes out at 2-4% the 'AI opponent beats the judge' beat deflates on stage and the team has no fallback story prepared.

Demo script cannot survive contact with a judge. 300 s with zero slack: a trackpad handoff to a stranger in an unfamiliar 3D UI (budgeted 30 s, realistically 60-90 s: mis-clicks, camera spin, 'which one is the dock?'), a 10 s live anneal that is dead air on a projector, a 25 s 'stretch' section that lists three features without showing any, and a 10 s limitations slide. The beats most likely to be cut by the clock are the ghost race and the held-out leaderboard, which are the two things that make it memorable and honest.

'Where is the AI?' is the first Q&A question at NexAI Hack and the current answer is a paragraph of defence. Simulated annealing is a legitimate classic-AI search method, but only if it is shown learning something frequency sorting cannot (affinity) AND the gain is on screen as a measured number on held-out orders. As written, the plan has the mechanism but no guarantee the number exists.

Graph distances: the plan says 'BFS/Dijkstra all-pairs'. BFS is wrong here because edges are weighted unequally (1.2 m bay pitch vs 4.5 m aisle pitch vs 3.0 m cross-aisles). Must be Dijkstra or Floyd-Warshall (121 nodes, trivial). A judge who asks 'how did you compute slot-to-slot distances?' and hears BFS will assume hop counts, not metres.

The on-screen counters conflate the 20 animated orders with the full-month headless totals. 'Every saved metre is measured on screen, not claimed' is literally false: 20 of ~2,000 orders are animated; the rest is headless. The banner disclosure helps, but a single counter that fills to monthly totals while 20 orders animate invites 'so the animation is theatre'.

Drag-to-slot via drei DragControls on an InstancedMesh is the kind of thing that works on the dev laptop and fails on the demo trackpad (DragControls targets Object3D children; instances need a proxy mesh). The demo script nevertheless says 'O drags WHITE HANGING HEART...' instead of using the click-click swap the plan itself designates as primary.

Version pins (three 0.186.1, fiber 9.8.2, drei 10.7.9, postprocessing 6.39.5 / @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1, vite 8.3.5, react 19.3.1, tailwind 4.3.3, motion 14.5.0, pandas 3.0.6) are asserted, not verified; @react-three/postprocessing peer ranges on three have broken installs before. Bloom is the single most cosmetic dependency and the most likely peer-dep casualty.

drei <Line> rebuilds LineGeometry whenever `points` changes; growing the points slice every frame to 'draw the path' is a per-frame geometry allocation that will stutter on an integrated GPU exactly when the camera is also tweening. Needs preallocated points with animated instanceCount/drawRange instead.

Human workload: the build plan has humans merging hourly from 22:00 to 14:45 with no sleep block, then doing a live 5-minute demo with a trackpad handoff and 3 minutes of Q&A about Held-Karp bitmask DP and Metropolis acceptance. Explainability of agent-written code is the stated judging criterion ('every team member must be able to explain') and tiredness is the way that fails.

Naming: the baseline is pure frequency-rank-to-nearest-slot (volume-based/COI-like), not ABC class-based storage. Calling it 'ABC' invites a pedantic correction from any supply-chain judge and signals the team learned the term tonight.
Affinity overlay as 'top-50 co-picked pairs drawn as glowing links' across 120 slots is a hairball on a projector; it will look like noise rather than explanation.

Indian framing is pasted on: hook says Blinkit dark store, data card says UK online gift retailer with wholesaler invoices. Both are true, but opening on Blinkit and then showing 'United Kingdom' in the order ticker 40 seconds later is the kind of mismatch a tired judge notices.

Coverage risk is stated but not quantified: the plan expects top-100 SKUs to cover 20-30% of lines. If it is 15%, the twin is replaying a thin slice of each wholesaler invoice and 'avg pick time per order' is dominated by 1-line orders with a forced return to dock. Honest, but the team must own the number before a judge computes it from the Data card.
fixes: Measure Annealed-vs-Baseline on the held-out half by hour 4 (before any scene polish). If gain >= 8%: keep the AI-opponent beat as is. If 3-8%: reframe the sentence to 'the baseline captures most of it; the annealer finds X% more from order affinity, and under batch picking (2 orders/trip) that grows to Y%' and build batch.ts first so Y exists. If < 3%: drop the 'AI opponent' framing, keep SA as a leaderboard row, and spend the beat on the ghost race and the judge's swap instead.

Add a second, defensible 'original' layout: catalogue order (SKUs slotted in StockCode order, aisle by aisle), i.e. what a warehouse does when nobody has slotted. Show Random (seed 42, mean +- sd over seeds 1-10) AND Catalogue as two 'original' rows so the straw-man question is answered before it is asked. Use Catalogue as the ghost in the race.

Cut the demo to three beats and give each slack: 0:00-0:20 hook; 0:20-0:45 data card + click a rack; 0:45-1:40 replay with self-drawing path; 1:40-2:30 slotting: ONE pre-highlighted click-click swap by the operator, delta goes green, then Auto-baseline flies boxes; 2:30-3:30 ghost race (Catalogue vs Baseline vs Annealed counters, minimap); 3:30-4:10 Anneal with a 5 s live budget while the precomputed 60 s curve is already drawn behind it, then the leaderboard with opt and held-out columns; 4:10-4:30 one stretch toggle (batch picking) with its measured number; 4:30-4:50 limitations + QR; 4:50-5:00 'the laptop is yours during Q&A'. Move the judge handoff into Q&A, where fumbling costs nothing and gives the team 3 minutes of goodwill.

Replace BFS with Floyd-Warshall over the 121-node weighted graph (or Dijkstra from each node). Add a vitest that (a) hand-checks 5 slot pairs on the toy layout against ruler distances and (b) asserts every edge of every routed path is an edge of the graph (no rack crossing), and say that test exists in Q&A.

Split the HUD counters: 'This replay (20 orders): 1.21 km vs 0.88 km' and 'Full month (headless, 2,0xx orders): 18.4 km vs 12.9 km'. Rewrite the one-liner to 'scored by the same simulation that drives the animation' instead of 'measured on screen'.

Make click-select then click-target swap the only interaction in the script; keep DragControls behind a flag and enable it only if it passes a trackpad test on the demo laptop by 09:00. Add a top-down orthographic preset so targets are large.

Hour 0: `npm view <pkg> version` for every pin, `npm ls three` to confirm one three instance, commit the lockfile. Make Bloom/SMAA an optional chunk that can be deleted in one commit; the demo must look good with Quality=Off.

PathLine: preallocate the full path points once per order and animate `geometry.instanceCount` (Line2 draws instanced segments) or a shader uniform `progress`; never mutate `points` per frame. Floor heat: one `instanceColor` buffer updated with needsUpdate per picked tile, not per frame.

Add October 2011 as a second held-out set in eval only (prep.py emits orders_2011-10.json; scripts/eval.ts scores the Nov-fitted layouts on it). One extra table row answers 'does a layout chosen on this month hold next month' better than the within-month split alone.
Rename 'ABC' to 'Baseline: fast movers nearest the dock (the brief's)' everywhere; mention in the README that this is volume-based slotting and ABC class-based storage is the coarser cousin.
Affinity overlay: show only the top-8 partners of the currently selected SKU, plus a side table; never 50 links at once.

Hook: open on 'in any fulfilment centre, travel is ~50% of a picker's time (Tompkins 2010, as cited in de Koster 2007)' and add dark stores in one clause; keep Blinkit for the LinkedIn post. Build the 4x8 dark-store preset only if everything else is frozen by 10:00.
Explicitly drop Customer_ID in prep.py and say so in data/README.md (no personal identifiers reach the public JSON).

Humans: 2 x 3 h sleep in shifts between 00:00 and 06:00. Agent commits on public feature branches satisfy the hourly-commit rule; humans merge at 02:00, 06:00, 09:00, 11:00 only. Each human owns 2 modules and writes the Q&A card for each from the merged code, not from the plan.
Replace the 2-second fps probe with a manual Quality default (Balanced) persisted in localStorage; the operator sets it before the slot. One fewer moving part at load.

Pre-write and rehearse the 20-second 'where is the AI' answer with a number in it: 'search-based optimisation (classic AI) that learns co-purchase structure from 2,0xx real orders and beats the frequency baseline by X% on orders it never saw; an LLM would be theatre for a combinatorial problem'.
steal_worthy: Ghost race: the before-layout picker walking the same orders as a translucent ghost beside the after-layout picker, with diverging counters and a 2D minimap mirror for the projector. Works for any before/after simulation (EV charging uncontrolled vs scheduled, VRP original vs re-planned, markdown policy A vs B).

One pure headless simulate() shared by scoring, animation, baseline, optimiser and `npm run eval`; the animation only replays what was already scored, with an on-screen banner stating 'animating 20 of N, totals from headless simulation'.

`npm run eval` writing eval/results.md with git commit hash and date, re-run in CI on every push so README/deck numbers are generated, never typed; deck numbers copied from that file at feature freeze.

Chronological held-out split with optimiser hyperparameters frozen in DEV_LOG before the first run on the held-out half, and in-sample vs held-out printed side by side with the sentence 'held-out gain is smaller; that is the honest number'.

Incremental delta evaluation via inverted index (SKU -> orders) so a single move re-scores only ~200 affected orders in milliseconds, giving sub-second feedback on a full month of data without a backend.

Zero-backend static deployment with a Cloudflare Pages mirror and `vite preview` on two laptops: no API keys, no cold starts, no rate limits, deterministic seeds displayed on screen so 'replay twice' gives identical numbers.
Seeded random 'original' reported as mean +- sd over seeds 1-10 so the comparison baseline is not cherry-picked.
Judge-plays-the-game beat (time-boxed into Q&A rather than the 5-minute slot) and the 'Mario Kart ghost for warehouses' one-sentence pitch that judges repeat to each other.
